text:
Devon: Heads up — after last night's quota-ui deploy, the eval-route default quota was set to 0 for a subset of internal eval routes. We're getting 429s across internal keys. Anyone oncall?

Maria: Saw the spike at 09:12 UTC, lots of 429s hitting /v1/generate?model=eval-lite from our internal test harness. Quick error sample: `{"status":429,"error":"rate_limited","message":"burst quota exceeded"}`. Stack shows enforcement code path hit. :eyes:

infra-bot: alert: quota_enforcement.high_429_rate org=internal-evals value=12.4% link=https://grafana.redwood/alerts/3821

Devon: My suspicion — the console migration that normalized legacy quotas had a mapping that treated null burst as 0. That migration ran with `apply-all` in the deploy. If true, that explains zeroing out many eval routes.

Ashok: Oof. Can we revert? I can push a rollback to console defaults and trigger propagation, but caches might keep old zeros for a bit.

Sara: On it. I sent a quick admin PATCH to set missing/zero bursts for any route with tag=eval -> `PATCH /admin/v1/orgs/internal/routes {"burst": 10}`. Pushing as a hotfix now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started patch rollout to admin-api (run id=deploy-20260318-3)

Kevin: Propagation started 09:20 UTC. Watching token-level logs: 429 rate dropped from 12.4% -> 2.1% in the first minute, now down to 0.7% at 09:28. Cache TTL meant a few keys still 429ing but trending down.

Maria: Confirmed downstream test harness passed after patch. We're still seeing a handful of consumer SDKs with retries, but overall impact contained.

Devon: Root cause summary: migration logic for legacy quotas had `if burst == null then burst = 0` to be explicit; for eval routes that should have defaulted to a nonzero emergency burst. The console's new 'apply-all' flow executed the script cluster-wide without the eval-specific guard.

Ashok: Created PR #2489 to add schema validation in the console UI and server-side guard to reject burst==0 for routes tagged as `eval` or `system-test`. Also adding a migration rollback job to set sensible defaults for null/0 cases.

Sara: I'll follow up with a quick postmortem bullet list: timeline, root cause, remediation (hotfix + PR), and three action items: 1) add canary for apply-all, 2) add preflight validation that prevents applying zero burst to any route type we consider critical, 3) add metric/alert for sudden mass-zero writes to quota table.

Devon: Also recommend adding a small integration test in the migration harness that fails the run if more than X routes end up with burst<=0.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0457 assigned to Platform Eng.

Kevin: Leaving a note: we should avoid using 0 as a sentinel for 'unset' in DB nullables. Make schema explicit (NULL = unset, not 0).

Maria: Thanks everyone — impact mostly internal but good catch before this affected customer-facing routes. I'll coordinate the postmortem doc and tag the SRE/console owners. :thumbsup:

Devon: Closing the looping alerts for now. We'll keep watch on the dashboard for 24h. If anything creeps up ping here and PD.
